prompt: For the data set $2$, $4$, $4$, $5$, $10$, which statement is true?

choices.label: The mean is greater than the median
The median is greater than the mean
The mean and median are equal
The mean is less than the smallest value

hint: Compute both, or reason from the shape: is there a value pulling one of them?

hints.text: Compute both, or reason from the shape: is there a value pulling one of them?
Mean $= 25 \div 5 = 5$; median is the middle value, $4$.

learningObjective: Compare mean and median for a skewed data set.
explanation: The values are already sorted, so the median is the third: $4$.
The mean exceeds the median because the value $10$ sits far above the rest and drags the mean up.

alternativeExplanations.title: Read the skew instead of computing
steps: The values cluster at $2$-$5$ with one straggler at $10$ — right-skewed.
The mean chases outliers; the median ignores them. So in a right-skewed set, mean > median.
Left-skewed reverses it. Knowing this rule answers most center-comparison questions without any arithmetic.
